headline: Endurance is sustained capacity—the ability to keep going when others stop
universal_truth: Persistence often matters more than intensity; what you can sustain determines what you achieve
fun_facts: Humans can outrun almost any animal over long distances—we're evolution's endurance specialists
Endurance training increases the number of mitochondria in your cells—literally more energy factories
Mental fatigue often hits before physical limits—your body can usually do more than your mind thinks
discussion_questions: Where does your endurance fail—physical, mental, emotional?
What determines how long you can sustain effort?
How do you build capacity for the long haul?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Sprints are dramatic, but races are won by those who keep going. Endurance is sustained capacity—the ability to maintain effort when others fade. Many endeavors are marathons, not sprints. Can you keep going?

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We often focus on peak performance, but sustained performance matters more. What builds endurance?

options.text: Endurance builds through sustained sub-maximal effort—not going all-out, but going consistently; training your systems to maintain output over time builds staying power
options.response: Yes. Endurance isn't built by sprinting until you collapse. It's built by sustained effort below maximum—training your body to keep delivering. Consistency, not intensity, builds stamina.

options.text: Some people just have more stamina
options.response: Genetics matter, but endurance is highly trainable—it responds to consistent practice...

q1.title: Sustainable Pace
q1.script: Endurance requires finding sustainable pace—effort you can maintain. Too fast, you burn out. Too slow, you don't progress. The art is finding the edge of sustainability.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Sustainable Pace"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Mental vs Physical
q2.script: Mental fatigue usually precedes physical exhaustion. Your body can often do more than your mind thinks. Training endurance partly means training your mind to keep going.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Long-Term Endeavors
q3.script: Most important things in life are endurance tests: careers, relationships, health. Can you keep going when enthusiasm fades? Endurance determines long-term success.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Persistence often matters more than intensity. What you can sustain determines what you achieve. Build endurance.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 305—welcome to November! Tomorrow, we'll explore bending without breaking—flexibility. Until then, consider your capacity for sustained effort.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Endurance Check - How Long Can You Go?
growTrack.activity: Where does your endurance fail—in work, exercise, relationships, focus? What's your sustainable pace? How could you train your capacity to sustain effort for longer periods?
